query: Were Thomas H. Ince and Joseph McGrath of the same nationality?

Thomas H. Ince was a pioneer film actor who worked as a screenwriter and director before becoming a prominent figure in the silent film industry. He studied at Glasgow School of Art in the late 1940s/early 1950s where his energy and talent was much admired by his contemporaries.

Joseph McGrath, on the other hand, is an American screenwriter who worked as a screenwriter before becoming a prominent figure in the silent film industry. He studied at Glasgow School of Art in the late 1940s/early 1950s where his energy and talent was much admired by his contemporaries.

So, while they share some similarities (both were born in Glasgow), they have distinct careers that set them apart from one another.
